title: The Complete Guide to Telegram Bot API Free (2026)
meta_description: What does Telegram Bot API Free cost in 2026 (spoiler: nothing), and how do you set it up properly? Covers free tiers, open-source alternatives and honest…
intro: This is the kind of post The Free Stack exists to write: a practical, no-fluff guide to telegram bot api free, assembled from free tiers, open-source projects and endpoints that ask for no API key at all.

We'll walk through Telegram Bot API, Bluesky At Protocol, Mastodon API, and Choose boring technology first — and finish with the questions people actually ask, so you can check before you buy anything. You shouldn't have to buy anything.

sections.heading: Telegram Bot API
paragraphs: First, the thing that actually matters: The Telegram Bot API is free, HTTP-based and needs nothing but a token from @BotFather.

The upshot: Create a bot in one message, then send and receive messages, create channels, and drive webhooks entirely over plain HTTPS. It is the cheapest 'social media' channel a self-publishing site can own, and this blog posts to it when a token is configured.
No signup wall, no credit card — just a README and some patience.
bullets: Message @BotFather and /newbot to get a token
Optionally set a webhook with setWebhook for incoming events

sections.heading: Bluesky At Protocol
paragraphs: The foundation looks like this: Bluesky runs on the open AT Protocol, whose public API is free — an account plus an app password is all a bot needs to post.

Concretely: createSession returns an access token, and app.bsky.feed.post publishes a post. No middleman, no paid 'basic tier' for your own account's posting, and the protocol is openly specified so the implementation is boring in the best way.
The links in the sources section go straight to the primary docs.

sections.heading: Mastodon API
paragraphs: Skip the fluff and start here: Mastodon's API is free and fully documented — any instance lets you register an app and post programmatically.

In practice that means: Create an app in your instance's developer settings, exchange it for a token, and the REST API handles statuses, follows and search. Because the whole platform is open source and federated, posting to it costs nothing and can point at an instance you run yourself.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.

sections.heading: Choose boring technology first
paragraphs: Here's the part most people get wrong. The best infrastructure for a side project is the least surprising kind: static files, a public repo, a free CDN in front of it.

In other words: Every exotic dependency is a future tax. If a free, open-source tool can serve the job, pick the one with the longest track record and the biggest community, and save the interesting experiments for the parts users actually touch.
If you only do one thing today, make it this one.
